en: The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
The Second Training Rule on Being Well-Restrained:
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks sat in inhabited areas playing with their hands and feet... [as before] ...
"The training is to be observed: 'I will sit well-restrained in inhabited areas.
One should sit in inhabited areas being well-restrained.
If one, out of disrespect, sits in an inhabited area while playing with one’s hand or foot, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
There is no offense if it was unintentional.
In the case of one who is lacking mindfulness, one who is unaware, or one who is ill.
"In the case of one who is insane,
or in the case of the first offender.
The sixth training rule is concluded.
